newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Anaconda says has native backing on Murrin.
newsitem.headline: Anaconda says has native backing on Murrin.

text.p: Anaconda Nickel Ltd shares were reinstated for Australian Stock Exchange trading early Thursday afternoon after the company said it had reached agreement with all Aboriginal groups for development of the Murrin Murrin nickel/cobalt project.
The stock was earlier suspended pending an announcement.
The A$900 million Murrin Murrin project is located east of the outback town of Leonora in Western Australia.

Andrew Forrest, Anaconda's chief executive officer and chairman of the Murrin Murrin joint-venture, said agreement had been reached with the final two Aboriginal groups, the Bibila-Lungutjarra Goolburthunoo people.

"A binding agreement was signed yesterday, clearing the way for the project to proceed with approval of the infrastructure, plant and tailing sites and the remaining Aboriginal heritage issues," he said in a statement.
Murrin Murrin is scheduled to come on stream at the end of 1998 and to reach production of 45,000 tonnes of nickel and 3,000 tonnes of cobalt in that year.
Glencore International AG of Switzerland, which has a 40 percent stake in Murrin Murrin and a 19.0 percent stake in Anaconda Nickel, has exclusive rights to sell the cobalt and nickel.
Anaconda has plans to expand production to 75,000 tonnes of nickel a year and 5,000 tonnes of cobalt once the base plant is commissioned.
In February Forrest called on the mining industry to reconcile its differences over aboriginal land rights.
Murrin Murrin would employ about 20 percent aboriginals out of a total workforce of about 350, he said.
Forrest said in February that Anaconda has reached its own agreements with aboriginal land claimants over tracts of the Murrin Murrin project.
